title: Scope mismatch — strong non-platform PM; target role requires platform/API strategy ownership

assessment.general_capability: Product management ownership — personally owning product strategy and roadmap for a product at meaningful scope with quantified outcomes.
assessment.target_specific_requirement: Platform PM Developer APIs (Senior) — personal ownership of platform/API strategy, developer-integration decisions, and ecosystem/interface direction. Owning an API as the delivery mechanism for a customer-facing capability is NOT the same as owning platform/API strategy.

seed_gap.gap_title: No evidence of platform/API strategy ownership
seed_gap.gap_description: Resume shows PM ownership of a reliability product but does not surface personal ownership of platform/API strategy, developer-integration decisions, or ecosystem direction. Target role requires owning platform/API strategy at scale.
seed_gap.recommended_fix: Establish whether the candidate has personally owned platform/API strategy decisions.

seed_analysis.positioning_summary: Senior PM for an internal reliability product with meaningful organizational scope. For a Platform PM target, the question is whether the candidate's API work extended to owning platform/API strategy or whether the API was simply a delivery mechanism for a customer-facing capability.

related_signals.rationale: Clear ownership of product strategy for Service Health.
API capability shipped but platform/API strategy ownership not surfaced.

persona.fallback_answer: Happy to be more specific — which part would you like me to dig into?

answer_rules.answer: I own product strategy and roadmap end-to-end for Lumen Service Health. The service is used by 132 internal service teams and surfaces live status to 1M+ enterprise customers. I make the prioritization and tradeoff calls.

I personally led a new API capability that lets enterprise customers plan around Lumen maintenance. It reduced support cases 17% in the first three months. I prioritized which service teams to onboard next; six more teams onboarded and support cases dropped a further 23%.

The hard part was prioritizing across 132 internal service teams with competing asks. I used customer-impact and support-case cost-of-delay as the ranking function and defended it in monthly business reviews with leadership.

17% support-case reduction in three months on the first wave. Six more service teams onboarded in the following quarter and support cases dropped a further 23%. I tracked and presented the metric monthly.

To be direct: no. I did not personally own platform or API strategy decisions. The API was the delivery mechanism for a customer-facing reliability capability I owned, not a platform play I set direction for. Developer-integration direction, ecosystem decisions, and platform investment priorities sat with the Lumen Platform team, not me.
